messages:
maria: noticed a weird spike in stream heartbeat billing for a small set of tenants, looks correlated with proxies that add x-hop-count.
aj: saw that too, dashboard shows stream.heartbeat.hopcount > 1 for ~2k requests/min from eu-west.
maria: exact issue — our quota attribution logic assumes hopcount==0 means client origin. proxies increment hopcount and we mark those as proxy-origin, which routes to fallback quota buckets. tenants get double-counted.
ken: oh neat, so proxy-incremented traffic is getting treated as coming from internal rather than customer? that would explain the apparent duplicate charge counts.
ui-liz: this also makes the console per-tenant timeline noisy. UX folks are seeing confusing drops when proxies pop in.
aj: i can reproduce locally by replaying a request with header `X-Stream-Hop: 1`. codepath: `stream_router->determine_origin()` basically checks hop==0 then tags origin=CLIENT else origin=PROXY.
maria: proposal: change the contract to include an explicit `X-Stream-Origin: client|edge|internal` header set by first hop. fallback to hop-count if missing for backward compat.
ken: sounds reasonable. but rolling that across edge proxies will take time. can we implement a shim server-side that treats hop-count==1 as client in the short term? risky but fast.
aj: i sketched a patch: if hop==1 and incoming `Via` contains our edge id pattern, treat as CLIENT_OR_PROXY_EDGE and attribute to tenant based on auth token. putting in feature flag `treat_single_hop_as_client`.
maria: +1 on feature flag. we need metric and alert to ensure we don't accidentally attribute true internal traffic. add `stream.attr.origin_override` metric.
sre-bot: alert: quota-variance:streaming detected for service=stream-router region=eu-west at 2025-05-12T09:12:03Z.
ken: for telemetry, add dimension `origin_header` that is raw header value and `origin_resolution` which is one of [client, edge_proxy, internal, override]. that helps dashboard filters.
ui-liz: console change: in per-tenant timeline, add small pill that shows "origin resolution" (hover explains hopcount/explicit header). Also add a toggle to collapse proxy-attributed counts.
aj: implementation plan: 1) server-side shim behind flag (canary 10% traffic) 2) telemetry dims + new metrics 3) console UI tweak 4) roll explicit header change to edge proxies 5) flip default and remove shim after 2 weeks stable.
maria: do we need to update audit logs? we should record when an override happened for compliance. add `stream.audit.origin_override=true/false`.
ken: perf wise, shim is cheap — single header parse. but need unit tests for replayed requests with manipulated headers. i'll add tests in stream-router suite.
ui-liz: can we mock this in dev console so product folks can see before rollout? a small toggle in staging would be enough.
aj: yes — I'll add a staging feature flag controlled by `features.streaming.origin_override`.
maria: question about quotas: should we backfill historical counts to dedupe past double-charges? probably not safe. we'll focus forward-looking correct attribution plus a retro report.
ken: agree. ops could run a one-off script that scans anomalies and flags customers to review billing, but no automated refunds without finance signoff.
sre-bot: deploybot: rolling canary for stream-router with flag=on to 10% — started at 2025-05-12T09:30Z by aj.
aj: patch PR coming, will include metrics, tests, and a small README for oncall.
maria: thanks — assign to me for review. can we also add a smoke dashboard widget `stream.attr.origin_override_rate` so oncall can see if the override is being used too much?
ken: done, i'll add the widget to the streaming SLO dashboard and pin to the top-right.
ui-liz: will mock UI pill and send screenshots in #eng-platform tomorrow.
aj: one more edge-case: multi-proxy chains where hop>1 but first hop set explicit header. shim must prefer explicit header always. will code that.
maria: ok, timeline: PR today, canary tonight, monitor metrics for 48h, UI in staging by EOD tomorrow, edge proxy header rollout next week.
ken: if we see any spike in `stream.attr.inconsistent_origin` we roll back.
ui-liz: lgtm from UX.
aj: pushing PR now -> https://git.redwood/stream-router/pull/3421 :small_fire:
maria: thanks all. I'll update the runbook with rollback criteria and billing notify draft.
ken: i'll add unit+integration tests, and a small lua shim for our edge proxies repo for when we start rolling headers.
ui-liz: uploaded mock screenshots: https://img.internal/redwood/mock-origin-pill.png
aj: canary metrics: `stream.attr.origin_override_rate` = 0.8% at 10% rollout, no increase in `stream.attr.inconsistent_origin` yet.
maria: good sign. leaving this thread open for 48h monitoring. ping @ken @aj if you see anything weird.
ken: noted. will set an alert to page if override_rate > 5% or inconsistent_origin > 0.1%.
ui-liz: thx, closing loop from UX side after staging review.
sre-bot: deploybot: canary finished, no errors detected, marking rollout as ongoing.
